# hostinger_vps_firewall_rule (Resource)

Manages a VPS firewall rule.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hostinger_vps_firewall" "example" {
  name = "My Firewall Group"
}

resource "hostinger_vps_firewall_rule" "example" {
  firewall_id   = hostinger_vps_firewall.example.id
  protocol      = "TCP"
  port          = "80"
  source        = "custom"
  source_detail = "any"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `firewall_id` (Number) ID of the firewall this rule belongs to
- `port` (String) Firewall rule destination port: single or port range
- `protocol` (String) Firewall rule protocol
- `source` (String) Firewall rule source. Can be `any` or `custom`
- `source_detail` (String) Firewall rule source detail. Can be `any` or IP address, CIDR or range

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `action` (String) Firewall rule action
- `id` (Number) Firewall rule ID

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = hostinger_vps_firewall_rule.example.id
  identity = {
    id          = 24541
    firewall_id = 65224
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `firewall_id` (Number) ID of the firewall this rule belongs to
- `id` (Number) Firewall rule ID

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform

  to = hostinger_vps_firewall_rule.example.id
  id = "65224/24541"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:
